title: The Nature of Superposition and Measurement in Quantum Mechanics
text:
Quantum mechanics fundamentally suggests that subatomic particles do not possess definite states until they are observed. Before measurement, a particle exists in a superposition—a probabilistic combination of all possible states simultaneously described by its wave function.

A crucial extension of this concept is quantum entanglement. When two or more particles become entangled, their fate becomes correlated such that measuring the state of one instantaneously dictates the state of the other, regardless of the distance separating them. This interconnectedness challenges classical notions of locality and remains a pivotal area of theoretical study.
